entrypoints.summary: Attacker-controlled recipient or identity text reaches the plugin parsing APIs when the plugin feature is enabled.
Public plugin constructors accept a plugin_name argument, including IdentityPluginV1::new and RecipientPluginV1::new.

affected_components.role: Parses plugin identifiers, derives executable names, resolves paths, and opens plugin connections.

code_slices.fixed: v0.11.1 adds valid_plugin_name, accepting ASCII alphanumerics and only +, -, ., _, and rejects invalid names at relevant boundaries.
code_slices.surrounding_context: Plugin discovery expects an age-plugin-{name} executable on PATH; the resolved path is retained in Plugin and supplied to Connection::open.
code_slices.vulnerable: v0.11.0 extracts a plugin name from structured recipient/identity input and uses binary_name followed by which::which and Connection::open without a plugin-name character allowlist.

observability.channel: process execution / fixed CLI error output
negative_controls: The v0.11.1 CLI fixture expects a failed status and a missing-plugin error for a slash-containing name.
No supplied artifact records a successful pre-fix execution run.
observability.positive_marker: The advisory describes execution of the selected binary with a plugin mode flag.

preconditions: The age plugin feature is enabled.
An attacker can supply recipient/identity text or a public API plugin_name argument.
For the documented UNIX attack path, an age-plugin-* directory exists in the working directory.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A plugin identifier with traversal-like slash-separated segments.
trigger_steps.summary: Supply a plugin name containing path separators through an affected API or CLI-mediated plugin selection path.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: The derived executable name is age-plugin-{attacker-controlled name}.
trigger_steps.summary: Cause plugin resolution and connection establishment for that identifier.

capabilities.concept: path-separator injection into plugin executable lookup

relation_candidates.dst: path-separator injection into plugin executable lookup
relation_candidates.rationale: Affected APIs accept attacker-controlled plugin names, and vulnerable parsing/resolution derives an executable lookup name from that identifier without character restriction.
The advisory states that a plugin name containing a path separator may execute an arbitrary binary and documents the UNIX directory precondition.
relation_candidates.src: path-separator injection into plugin executable lookup

relation_candidates.rationale: The patch introduces an ASCII character allowlist and applies it before plugin names are accepted through parsing and related paths.
relation_candidates.src: path-separator injection into plugin executable lookup

impact.affected_asset: The host process's executable-launch authority and the confidentiality/integrity boundary of data supplied to the plugin protocol.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause the plugin resolver to treat path-separator-bearing identifier content as part of an executable lookup target.
impact.security_effect: Arbitrary binary execution under the age/rage process context, conditional on the advisory's documented UNIX working-directory prerequisite.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker-controlled recipient, identity, or public constructor plugin name supplies the plugin identifier while the plugin feature is enabled.

In v0.11.0, identity parsing extracts the plugin-name portion of a Bech32 HRP into a String without restricting path-separator characters; the analogous recipient parsing is part of the affected API scope.
Plugin resolution formats the supplied name as age-plugin-{name}, passes it to which::which, retains the resolved path, and opens a plugin Connection using that path.

A path separator in the plugin name may allow arbitrary-binary execution; on UNIX, the documented success condition includes an age-plugin-* directory in the working directory. The executed binary receives a recipient-v1 or identity-v1 mode flag and constrained protocol input on stdin.

failure.operation: Executable lookup followed by plugin connection opening on the path resolved from age-plugin-{attacker-controlled name}.

primary_invariant.statement: A plugin identifier used to derive an executable lookup name must contain only ASCII alphanumeric characters or +, -, ., and _.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The vulnerable parser retained an attacker-provided HRP suffix as the plugin name without enforcing a non-path identifier character domain before executable lookup.

quality.review_notes: Primary vulnerable source, fixed source/patch, maintainer advisory, and negative regression oracles were inspected. The tests define rejection contracts only; no pre-fix execution trace or successful exploit run is present. Arbitrary-execution language is therefore advisory-grounded and conditional on the stated UNIX working-directory prerequisite.

remediation.invariant_restored: Names accepted as plugin identifiers are restricted to ASCII alphanumerics plus +, -, ., and _, preventing path separators from reaching derived executable lookup names.
mitigation_classes: ASCII allowlist enforcement for plugin identifiers
rejection at parser and public constructor boundaries

target.component: age plugin resolution and connection subsystem

oracle.channel: Rust API tests and rage CLI fixture
oracle.expected_negative: A slash-containing plugin name is not accepted as a plugin identifier and does not advance to successful plugin resolution/connection.
oracle.expected_positive: The fixed implementation rejects an invalid plugin name containing path-like characters with the documented error behavior.
